# Story 01 — Sign-in issues a token; a guarded route resolves it (Story: CRM-41)

## Prerequisites

- PLATFORM-4-API (`api/src/app.js`) is complete: `createApp(deps)` accepts `deps.subjectResolver` and mounts it via `attachSubject` before the versioned router (`api/src/app.js` lines 37–41). This story supplies the real resolver.
- Migration `0005__users.sql` is applied and `hashPassword` is exported from `api/src/platform/db/seed.js` line 37. The seeded admin row is what the first acceptance criterion signs in as (`api/src/platform/db/seed.js` lines 42–55).
- Coordinate with `IDENTITY-1-WEB (CRM-42)` — it will consume the JSON shape `{ token, user: { id, role, name } }` this story ships; do not add a field the intake does not name.
- **Read first:** `.squad/plan-lessons.md`, in particular **L-9** (never echo submitted values in error bodies), **L-10 / L-13** (do not hand-roll source scans), **L-11** (only the eight statuses in `DOCUMENTED`), **L-16** (prove the guard fails on purpose before ticking the box).

## Story Goal

Add the first `api/src/features/identity/` feature. A staff account signs in with email + password against the seeded row and receives an opaque token plus their `{ id, role, name }`. A guarded route (`GET /me`) uses a **new subject resolver** — wired into `createApp` from `server.js` — that reads the token, verifies its HMAC-SHA256 signature and expiry, loads the user, and returns the row **without** `password_hash`.

Rules owned:

- **I-3** — staff accounts are created by an admin; the first admin comes from the seed. **This story never creates a user**; sign-in only reads the seeded row.
- **SC-2** — every rule is enforced in the API. The validation, timing-safe comparison, "disabled/deleted → 401", token expiry, and signature check all live in the API; the web client will trust the response.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- The sign-in **screen** — IDENTITY-1-WEB (CRM-42).
- Creating / disabling / re-enabling accounts, role changes — IDENTITY-2-API (CRM-44).
- Rate limiting on repeated failures — IDENTITY-4-API (CRM-47). Do **not** issue 429 here.
- Assignable-agents list — IDENTITY-5-API (CRM-48).
- Password change / reset / session revocation — IDENTITY-6/7/8.
- Refresh tokens. One token with an expiry; a later story can argue for refresh.
- Customer sign-in and the portal.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** the default `attachSubject()` resolver returns `null` (`api/src/platform/http/permission.js` line 15). Every guarded call 401s. There is no sign-in route.
- **New behaviour:** `POST /api/v1/sign-in` accepts `{ email, password }` and answers `200 { token, user: { id, role, name } }` on success, `401 { code: 'UNAUTHENTICATED', requestId }` on failure — the same body for wrong password, unknown email, disabled account (any non-null `deleted_at`), or bad token. `GET /api/v1/me` is guarded by `requireSubject()` and answers `200 { id, role, name }`.

Read `SIGN_IN_TOKEN_SECRET` from `process.env` **once**, alongside `dbPath`. Rules:

- Otherwise (development): fall back to a **per-boot** random 32-byte hex secret from `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')` and `console.warn('SIGN_IN_TOKEN_SECRET not set; issuing a random secret for this process. Tokens will not survive a restart.')`. Comment says exactly why this is honest for dev and wrong for prod.

Export as `config.signInTokenSecret`. Keep the object `Object.freeze`d.

### 2 — Feature scaffolding under `api/src/features/identity/`

Create the folder and these files. `index.js` is the **only** external entry point (`docs/architecture.md` line 33 onward).

#### `api/src/features/identity/index.js`

```js
// The single export for the identity feature.
//   identityRouter(deps)     - mounted under the v1 router in app.js
//   identitySubjectResolver(deps) - passed as deps.subjectResolver to createApp
// Anything else this feature owns is internal.
export { identityRouter } from './identity.routes.js';
export { identitySubjectResolver } from './identity.subject-resolver.js';
```

#### `api/src/features/identity/identity.rules.js`

The **pure** part; no I/O, no `db`, no `req`/`res`.

- `verifyPassword(plaintext, stored)` — parses `salt:hash` hex, re-derives with `scryptSync(plaintext, salt, 64)` and compares with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Returns a boolean; **never** throws on bad shape (returns `false`), so a malformed row is a 401, not a 500. Comment: this is the other half of `hashPassword` in `api/src/platform/db/seed.js` line 37; it lives here because the feature owns the format now.
- `DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH` — a compile-time constant produced once from a known plaintext via `hashPassword`. Comment: **do not delete** — it is the target of the constant-time comparison performed when no row is found, so the timing of the "unknown email" branch matches the "wrong password" branch (intake: Timing).
- `signToken({ sub, role, exp }, secret)` — builds `base64url(JSON.stringify(payload)) + '.' + base64url(hmacSha256(payload, secret))`. Payload is exactly `{ sub, role, exp }`; `exp` is unix seconds. Algorithm and format are hard-coded — no algorithm header, no `alg: none` foothold. Comment names the algorithm and cites `node:crypto`.
- `verifyToken(raw, secret, { now = () => Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) })` — splits once; if the shape is wrong returns `null`. Recomputes the HMAC, compares with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers only (unequal-length returns `null`). Parses the payload JSON in a try/catch; returns `null` on any parse error. Returns `null` if `exp <= now()`. Otherwise returns the payload.
- `TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60 * 8` (eight hours). Comment: this is the whole session; refresh tokens are IDENTITY-6+.

#### `api/src/features/identity/identity.repository.js`

The **only** file in the feature that touches SQL (`docs/architecture.md` line 40).

- `findLiveUserByEmail(db, email)` — `SELECT id, email, password_hash, name, role FROM users WHERE email = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL LIMIT 1`. Returns the row or `undefined`. Comment: relies on `users_email_uniq` being partial on `deleted_at IS NULL` (migration 0005 lines 12–16).
- `findLiveUserById(db, id)` — `SELECT id, name, role FROM users WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL LIMIT 1`. **`password_hash` is not in the projection.** Comment: it cannot be returned to a client, so it does not leave the repository.

Prepared statements are created lazily against the `db` handle passed in (SQLite via `node:sqlite`, per `docs/architecture.md`; do not import a client).

#### `api/src/features/identity/identity.service.js`

- `createIdentityService({ db, secret, now })`
- `.signIn({ email, password })`:
  1. Validate the body **before** authenticating (intake: "Validation before authentication"). Missing or non-string `email` / `password`, or `email` not matching a minimal shape check (contains `@`, length ≤ 254), or `password.length === 0` → throw `unprocessable([...offendingFieldNames])` — **never** include the submitted value (L-9, and the constructor already filters non-strings, `api/src/platform/http/errors.js` line 52).
  2. Normalise `email = email.trim().toLowerCase()` before lookup (the column is `COLLATE NOCASE`, but normalising keeps the audit log deterministic in later stories).
  3. `const row = findLiveUserByEmail(db, email)`.
  4. `const ok = row ? verifyPassword(password, row.password_hash) : verifyPassword(password, DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH)`.
     Comment beside this line: **do not delete**. When the email is unknown we still hash a candidate against a dummy so the wrong-email path and the wrong-password path take the same time. This looks like pointless work and is not.
  5. If `!row || !ok` → throw `new HttpError(401, 'UNAUTHENTICATED')`. The message is intentionally identical for wrong password, unknown email, and soft-deleted account.
  6. Otherwise return `{ token: signToken({ sub: row.id, role: row.role, exp: now() + TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS }, secret), user: { id: row.id, role: row.role, name: row.name } }`. **`password_hash` is not in scope of the return** — the projection in the repository already omitted it, so a future edit cannot leak it by copying the row wholesale.
- `.me(subject)` → returns `subject` unchanged; the resolver already shaped it.

#### `api/src/features/identity/identity.subject-resolver.js`

- `identitySubjectResolver({ db, secret, now })` returns an `async (req) => …` suitable to be passed to `createApp({ subjectResolver })` (matches the shape `attachSubject` accepts, `api/src/platform/http/permission.js` line 15).
- Reads the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. If it is missing, malformed, does not start with `Bearer `, or has multiple spaces after the scheme, returns `null` (the seam turns null into `req.subject = null`; `requireSubject()` decides on the 401).
- Calls `verifyToken(raw, secret, { now })`. If it returns `null`, the resolver returns `null` — a tampered / expired / foreign-signed token is indistinguishable from no token, both become 401 at the guard (matches acceptance criterion 5).
- Otherwise loads the user with `findLiveUserById(db, payload.sub)`. If the row is missing or soft-deleted, returns `null` — a token issued to a since-deleted user must not resolve.
- Returns `{ id: row.id, role: row.role, name: row.name }`. **Never** returns `password_hash`.
- The resolver **must not throw**. Any unexpected exception becomes `next(err)` inside `attachSubject` (`permission.js` lines 21–23), which the terminal handler coerces to 500. Wrap the payload lookup in a try/catch that returns `null` on unexpected errors and logs a message with the request id — never the token.

#### `api/src/features/identity/identity.routes.js`

- `identityRouter({ db, secret, now })` builds and returns an `express.Router()`:
  - `POST /sign-in` → parses `req.body`, calls `service.signIn(...)`, `res.status(200).json(result)`.
  - `GET /me`, guarded by `requireSubject()`, → `res.json(req.subject)`.
- Both handlers are `async` and let thrown `HttpError` / `ValidationError` propagate to `errorHandler` (`api/src/platform/http/errors.js` lines 74–91) — do not `try/catch` for the happy path.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty / non-JSON body on `POST /sign-in`** — caught by `jsonBodyErrors()` (`api/src/app.js` line 35) as 400 `MALFORMED_BODY`; the service is not reached.
- **Body is JSON but missing a field** — service throws `unprocessable(['email'])` (or `['password']`, or both). 422; body carries the field names only, never the value (`errors.js` lines 49–56, L-9).
- **Body has extra fields** — silently ignored. The service reads only `email` and `password`.
- **Unicode email / mixed case** — `email` column is `COLLATE NOCASE` (migration 0005 line 3), and the service `toLowerCase().trim()`s before lookup, so `Admin@Example.com ` matches the seeded `admin@example.com`.
- **Unknown email** — repository returns `undefined`; service still runs `verifyPassword` against `DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH` (identity.rules.js) so the timing does not leak the account's existence. 401.
- **Wrong password** — same 401, same body, same `Content-Type`, same shape. Verified by an assertion that reads both responses.
- **Soft-deleted admin** — repository query filters `deleted_at IS NULL`, so a `deleted_at != NULL` row is invisible; sign-in returns 401 identical to unknown email. Verified by a test that soft-deletes the seeded admin, then signs in.
- **Token missing / not `Bearer`** — resolver returns `null`; guard returns 401.
- **Token whose signature was tampered** — HMAC recompute mismatches; `verifyToken` returns `null`; 401. No subject resolved (verified by asserting the handler did not run).
- **Token whose payload was tampered but signature was re-computed against a different secret** — HMAC mismatches against the correct secret; `verifyToken` returns `null`; 401.
- **Expired token** — `exp <= now()`; `verifyToken` returns `null`; 401. Test injects `now` in the resolver so the token can be produced with a past `exp` without waiting.
- **Token for a since-deleted subject** — resolver loads the user, finds nothing, returns `null`; 401.
- **Malformed `password_hash` in the DB** — `verifyPassword` returns `false` rather than throwing; the account cannot sign in; 401. Prevents a corrupt row from surfacing as 500.
- **`SIGN_IN_TOKEN_SECRET` missing in production** — `config` throws at module load; the process refuses to start. A running process cannot silently issue tokens nobody can verify after restart.
- **Same password stored twice** — `hashPassword` reads a fresh salt each call (`seed.js` line 38); the two hashes differ. Asserted by a unit test in the feature test file.
- **Concurrent sign-ins** — the service is stateless; `db.prepare` is safe on `node:sqlite`. Nothing to synchronise.
- **429** — **not issued here.** Rate limiting is IDENTITY-4-API's job; if it appeared now the contract test would still accept 429 (it is in `DOCUMENTED`) but the intake forbids inventing half of a rule.

## Test Plan

All tests are `node --test` against `:memory:` with `server.listen(0)` and built-in `fetch`, matching `api/src/app.test.js` and `api/src/platform/db/seed.test.js`.

1. **`api/src/features/identity/identity.rules.test.js`** — unit:
   - `hashPassword` (imported from `../../platform/db/seed.js`) then `verifyPassword` round-trips.
   - The same plaintext hashed twice produces two different `salt:hash` strings and both verify.
   - `verifyPassword('anything', 'garbage-not-colon-separated')` returns `false` and does not throw.
   - `signToken` then `verifyToken` round-trips with the same secret and returns the payload.
   - `verifyToken` returns `null` for: a token signed by a different secret; a token whose payload byte was flipped; a token with `exp` in the past; a token missing the `.`; a token whose base64 decoding fails.
   - `verifyToken` uses `timingSafeEqual` — assert by inspecting behaviour (equal-length wrong signature returns `null` without throwing).

2. **`api/src/features/identity/identity.service.test.js`** — service against a real `:memory:` DB and `runMigrations` + `seed`:
   - Seeded admin signs in with the seed's returned `adminPassword` → `{ token, user: { id, role, name } }`; assert `user` has exactly those three keys (no `password_hash`, no `email`, no `created_at`).
   - Wrong password → 401 with body `{ code: 'UNAUTHENTICATED', requestId }`.
   - Unknown email → 401 with the same body shape and the same `code`.
   - Soft-delete the admin (`UPDATE users SET deleted_at = ? WHERE email = ?`), then sign in with the right password → 401, same body.
   - Missing / non-string `email` or `password` → 422 with `fields` containing the offending name(s) and **no submitted value anywhere in the JSON**. Assert by re-serialising the response and searching for the submitted password substring — it must not appear (L-9).

3. **`api/src/features/identity/identity.routes.test.js`** — end-to-end through `createApp`:
   - Boot with `subjectResolver: identitySubjectResolver({ db, secret, now })` and `mountFeatures: (v1) => v1.use(identityRouter({ db, secret, now }))`.
   - `POST /api/v1/sign-in` → 200; capture the token.
   - `GET /api/v1/me` without `Authorization` → 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.
   - `GET /api/v1/me` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` → 200 with `{ id, role, name }` matching the seeded admin.
   - `GET /api/v1/me` with `Authorization: Bearer <token with a flipped byte in the payload>` → 401 and asserts the underlying handler did **not** run (mirror the `handlerRan` sentinel in `api/src/app.test.js` lines 81–93 — mount a sibling probe route if needed).
   - `GET /api/v1/me` with a token whose `exp` is in the past → 401. Build the token with the same `signToken` using a `now` returning e.g. `Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) - 3600 - TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS`.
   - `GET /api/v1/me` with a token signed by a **different** secret → 401.
   - `POST /api/v1/sign-in` timing sanity check — call the endpoint 5 times with an unknown email and 5 times with the seeded email and a wrong password; assert both medians are within the same order of magnitude (loose bound, avoids flake). Comment: this is a smoke test, not a defence — the actual defence is the dummy verify.

4. **`api/openapi.json`** contract regression — `api/src/platform/http/openapi-contract.test.js` (unchanged) must stay green with the two new entries. Run it after each edit; a red run names the offender.

5. **`api/src/app.test.js`** — add one test that boots `createApp({ mountFeatures })` (the new seam), asserts a mounted feature route is served under the prefix, and asserts an unrelated `mountTestRoutes` mount still works alongside it (proves L-12: the previous seam did not move, only gained a sibling).

**No test may:**

- grep the source tree for symbols (L-10, L-13). All invariants — "no `password_hash` in a response", "no submitted value in a 422 body" — are asserted by reading the actual HTTP response.
- assert on the token's inner structure. The token is opaque to the client; the round-trip through `verifyToken` is the whole contract.
- introduce a new status code. Only `DOCUMENTED` (`errors.js` lines 15–24) is legal (L-11).

## Migration / Rollback

No new migration. Migration `0005__users.sql` is the users table and it already exists.

Rollback of this story is delete-only: remove the feature folder, revert `api/openapi.json`, `api/src/server.js`, `api/src/app.js`, `api/src/platform/config/index.js`, and `.env.example`. No data lives outside seeded rows; nothing needs a backfill.

**Half-applied risk:** if `SIGN_IN_TOKEN_SECRET` is present in production but the code is reverted, no harm — the env var goes unread. If the code is deployed **without** the env var in production, the process throws at boot (by design), and the deploy fails loudly instead of silently issuing per-boot secrets.

## Verification Steps

1. **Backend runs:** in `api/`, `NODE_ENV=test node --test 'src/**/*.test.js'`. All existing tests plus the new ones pass. The pre-existing 82 tests must not regress (L-16).
2. **Backend builds:** in `api/`, `node --check src/features/identity/*.js` for each file (there is no separate build; `--check` is the syntax verifier).
3. **Contract test proves it fails on drift:** delete one of the two new `paths` entries in `api/openapi.json`, re-run the tests, watch `api/src/platform/http/openapi-contract.test.js` name the offending route, restore the entry, re-run green (L-16).
4. **Auth actually gates:** temporarily replace `subjectResolver` in `api/src/server.js` with `undefined`, boot with `node src/server.js`, `curl http://127.0.0.1:PORT/api/v1/me`, observe 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, restore.
5. **Prod-secret guard actually fires:** in a scratch shell, `NODE_ENV=production node -e "import('./src/platform/config/index.js')"` with `SIGN_IN_TOKEN_SECRET` unset — process throws with a message naming the env var.
6. **Regression:** `grep -R "password_hash" api/src/features/` returns matches only in `identity.repository.js` (the `findLiveUserByEmail` projection). It must **not** appear in `identity.service.js`, `identity.routes.js`, `identity.subject-resolver.js`, or any test's expected response body.
7. **No-AI-attribution guard:** `git log -n 20 --pretty=%B | grep -Ei 'claude|gpt|copilot|assistant|ai-generated' && exit 1 || echo ok` for the commits this story adds, and the existing `no-ai-attribution.test.js` stays green.
8. **Manual smoke:** `npm run seed` (or equivalent) prints the admin email + password; `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:PORT/api/v1/sign-in -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"…","password":"…"}'` returns `{ token, user }`; the same token used as `Authorization: Bearer …` on `/api/v1/me` returns `{ id, role, name }`.
